podcast.title: Prime Minister's Britpop Fandom (1997)
podcast.body: Upon his election as Prime Minister, Tony Blair, who had played in a rock band during university and loved Britpop, invited figures like Noel Gallagher to 10 Downing Street. This interaction, however, created "bad optics" for Noel, suggesting that the "music of the people" had been co-opted by the establishment. "Tony Blair was elected Prime Minister. Back in university, he played an rock band, and he loved Brit Pop. He even invited people like Noel Gallagher round to 10 Downing Street for a chat and a glass of wine."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Astrophysicist and Academic Chancellor
xref.body: Brian May is a distinguished physicist with a doctorate earned for his work titled "A Survey of Radio Velocities in the Zodiacal Dust Cloud." He currently holds the prestigious position of chancellor at Liverpool University, succeeding Cherie Blair (Tony Blair's wife) in this role. "He's a full fledged physicist with a doctorate based on his work called a survey of radio velocities in the zodiacal dust cloud."

xref.title: Cocaine at 10 Downing Street
xref.body: Noel Gallagher, known for never going without his cocaine, once slipped into the bathroom reserved for the Queen at 10 Downing Street during a party hosted by Prime Minister Tony Blair to do a couple of "rails." "When he was invited to a party at 10 Downing Street by the then-New Prime Minister Tony Blair, he actually slipped into the bathroom that's reserved for official visits by the queen and did a couple of rails."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Establishment Co-option
xref.body: Noel Gallagher was invited to 10 Downing Street by Prime Minister Tony Blair, who was a Britpop fan. This created "bad optics" for Noel, making the "music of the people" appear co-opted by the establishment and government. "All it said was that this music of the people had been co-opted by the establishment and the government."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
